name: TMCO Inc
old_description: When Roland Temme founded TMCO in 1974, he started with eight simple machines housed in a 742-square-foot machine shop located between the railroad tracks in Lincoln, Nebraska.
about:
TMCO Inc was founded in 1974 by Roland Temme in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company began with eight machines in a 742-square-foot machine shop situated between railroad tracks. Today, the business is led by CEO Diane Temme Stinton and President Anwar Rida, with Temme serving as chairman emeritus.

The company operates a 300,000-square-foot production facility offering full-service metal manufacturing. Capabilities include engineering, CNC machining (turning and milling), sheet metal and tube fabrication, robotic and manual welding, powder coating, and assembly. TMCO's concept-to-completion model keeps all processes in-house, from prototyping through finishing.

TMCO serves a global customer base, shipping to Canada, Mexico, Germany, and across the United States. Its most commonly served industries are agriculture and farming — producing components for irrigation pivots and farm equipment — and energy, where it manufactures parts for natural gas solutions. The company works with OEMs on complex components and turnkey projects.

TMCO emphasizes continual reinvestment in advanced equipment and workforce training to maintain quality and on-time delivery. Its engineering team partners with customers to solve manufacturability challenges, and the company states that eliminating third-party processing shortens lead times and improves control over the product lifecycle.
